title: High action among the great bassists
summary: Stewart always played with high action; he recalls that Braud, Blanton, Pettiford and Page did too, giving a big sound.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Have you always played with your action
Yes, always.
Now, when you were coming along, did most bass players -- as we know, bass players today, in order to play at the speed that they like to play, --
That's right, yeah.
-- they play in the range, play it with a lot of those high notes, they tend to play with the action pretty close to the finger board.
That's right.
But when you were coming up, did the guys used to tend to play with the action higher?
No, they -- not very many, hardly any fellas played with a high action.
Oh, they played with theirs close, too?
Oh, yes, yes. I remember though, like Brava?
Wellman
Uh-huh.
He had high action. A few of the fellas did.
What about Blanton? Did Blanton?
Blanton, I think he had high action also, yes.
What about Pettiford?
Pettiford? Come to think of it, he had
high action, yes.
So most of the guys then -- so almost all the guys that had -- what about Walter Page?
Walter Page? Yes, ... comes back to me as time goes by, yes, and we think about those days.
So then most of those guys played -- so most of the guys that got that big sound out of the instrument used the high action.
High action. That was it, yes.
